## Analysis

**Test image observations:**
- Field-level view of soybean plants
- Dead brown/tan leaves **remaining attached** to stems (not dropped)
- Stems appearing bleached/white on dying plants
- Patches of dying plants interspersed with healthy green plants
- Consistent with mid-to-late season disease

**Candidate evaluation:**

- **White_Mold**: Best match. The top-right panel of the White_Mold collage shows an almost identical field view — patches of dying plants with dead leaves still attached and bleached white stems. The key diagnostic "dead leaves remaining attached to stems while turning brown" and bleached white stem appearance is clearly visible in the test image.

- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Field view is similar but SDS shows interveinal chlorosis/yellowing pattern on leaves — the test image shows more complete browning and dead leaf retention, not the yellowing mottled leaves of SDS.

- **Charcoal_Rot**: The field-level view shows more complete defoliation with only bleached stems remaining — the test image retains many dead leaves on the plant.

- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Shows more uniform patch die-off with more yellow coloring, and the pith browning is the diagnostic feature (internal), not the field appearance.

- **Soybean_rust**: Shows more uniform senescence across the whole field, not the patchy dying with attached dead leaves pattern.

The dead-leaf-retention on bleached stems in a field with green surrounding plants is the hallmark of White_Mold.
